ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, lines AB and CD intersect at point O, $\angle DOE = 90^\circ$, OD bisects $\angle BOF$, $\angle BOE = 50^\circ$. What is the degree measure of $\angle AOC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\angle DOE=90^\circ$, $\angle BOE=50^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BOD=\angle DOE-\angle BOE=40^\circ$, $\angle AOD=180^\circ-\angle BOD=140^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle AOC=180^\circ-\angle AOD=\boxed{40^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, point O is the common endpoint of multiple rays; AB is an oblique straight line passing through O, with A at the lower left and B at the upper right; CD is a horizontal straight line passing through O, with C on the left side and D on the right side. Therefore ∠BOD and ∠AOC are a pair of vertical angles. The figure also draws OE vertically upward and OD horizontally to the right, with a right-angle mark between the two, corresponding to ∠DOE = 90°; ray OB is located inside ∠DOE. The problem text gives ∠BOE = 50°. Reasoning: because OB is inside ∠DOE, ∠DOE = ∠BOE + ∠BOD. Thus ∠BOD = 90° - 50° = 40°. Also because ∠AOC and ∠BOD are vertical angles, and vertical angles are equal, ∠AOC = 40°.
